subject: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler - follow-up & POC next steps

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jared Lim <jared.lim@acme.com>

Subject: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler - follow-up & POC next steps

Hey Jared —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- What we heard: Acme is evaluating options to support a marketing-driven traffic spike (short multi-day bursts) and long-term steady-state inference for your chat assistant. Main concerns were capacity guarantees, predictable unit cost, and a simple procurement path.
- How Redwood differentiates vs hyperscalers: Reserved/dedicated GPU pools with explicit capacity guarantees and predictable throughput (no noisy neighbor preemption), workload-aware batching and KV caching to reduce per-token cost, and a unified API/rollout model so you can pin model versions across environments. Hyperscalers typically rely on preemptible/spot capacity or shared autoscaling that can introduce risk during spikes unless you do expensive reserved instances yourself.

Suggested POC tests (we can run these in parallel):
1) Throughput & burst: reserve a small dedicated pool (e.g., 4 A10/H100-equivalent GPUs) and run a 6-8 hour burst to simulate your marketing spike.
2) Failover & fallback: throttle dedicated pool and confirm automatic fallback to hosted capacity (with graceful degradation) and measure latency impact.
3) Unit economics: run matched request mixes on both Redwood Dedicated and your hyperscaler reserved config to compare per-token cost including batching effects.

Requested next items from your side:
- Confirm stakeholders (procurement, infra) and a target week for the POC.
- Any compliance or data residency constraints (if we need a VPC or private deployment).
- A point of contact at procurement so we can share draft MSA + SOW and standard SLA language.

If useful, I can put together a one-page POC plan and a short SLA draft — Laura (cc'd) can own the test scaffolding. Are you available for a 30-min sync on Thursday 10/22 to lock the plan?

Thanks,

Markus Klein
Senior Account Executive

Hi Jared / Markus —

Thanks for the context. Quick notes and the proposed POC test plan (attached):

POC test summary (target week 10/26):
- Reserved pool: 4 x H100-equivalent GPUs reserved for 72 hours (24h warm-up + 48h storm simulation). We can provision within 48 hours once contract is signed; for guaranteed hold we request a signed SOW confirming reserved window.
- Throughput test: synthetic replay of your traffic shape (mix of 1–3k token requests) to validate sustained throughput and latency SLOs.
- Burst scenario: run a 6-hour spike at 3x baseline to validate autoscaling/fallback behavior and measure tail latencies.
- Failover: intentionally throttle the dedicated pool to verify automatic fallback to our hosted tier and observe quality/latency degradation.
- Cost benchmark: run identical request traces against your hyperscaler reserved config (you can share a billing/export sample) and our Dedicated pool; we’ll include batching and KV-cache effects in the analysis.

Capacity & SLA notes:
- We offer a reserved-dedicated contract with capacity guarantees for the reserved window. If Redwood fails to deliver reserved capacity during the agreed window, we apply service credits (tiered by severity) and operational escalation commitments. Exact credit terms are in the attached SLA PDF.
- Minimum lead time: 48 hours to provision if capacity is available in our region; 5–10 business days for formal procurement lead time if a contract negotiation is required.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sla.pdf (SLA summary), acme-poc-test-plan.md (detailed test steps).

Next steps:
1) Markus to share one-pager and draft MSA/SOW with procurement.
2) Acme to confirm procurement contact and sign SOW to lock the 10/26 window (or propose alternate dates).
3) We run the POC and deliver a short report with throughput/cost comparisons.

I’ll also drop a calendar invite for Thu 10/22 10:00am PT. If you want additional nondisclosure or compliance paperwork for the POC, let us know and we’ll route that to our legal/compliance team.

Best,
